title: improve-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion
author: Riley Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce token-level cost and p99 latency for quantized models by fusing dequantization and SmoothQuant scaling into the INT8/FP8 kernel hot path, and make small scheduler + KV-cache adjustments to preserve latency SLOs during continuous batching. Change summary: add fused_dequant_smoothquant kernels for INT8 and FP8 backends with specialized micro-kernels and vectorized paths; introduce a fusion-aware execution path selector in the kernel dispatcher; add alignment-aware buffer allocation to avoid extra copies; update scheduler to prefer low-latency lanes when fused kernels are available; make KV-cache reads zero-copy when input layouts match the fused kernel expectations; add benchmarks and CI perf tests. Results: microbenchmarks on A100 and H100 show up to 1.9x throughput for medium-length sequences (seq_len=512, batch=8) and median p99 latency reduction of ~25% on common chat workloads with base-8 and fp8 quantized checked models; end-to-end regression tests show no degradation in output similarity (Delta BLEU<0.1 point on eval set). Backwards compatibility: the new path is opt-in via a runtime flag (env REDWOOD_QUANT_FUSION=1) and disabled by default until we finish rollout and cross-validate against production traces. Testing: unit tests for fused kernels, integration tests for scheduling interactions, end-to-end perf harness with golden outputs, and a canary on Dedicated. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> global. Checklist: [x] micro-kernels implemented and benchmarked; [x] scheduler tweaks added; [x] KV-cache zero-copy path added; [x] perf tests added; [x] docs and release notes updated; [x] feature gated. Notes: kept separate fallback path for legacy models and added telemetry to track fusion hits/misses.

review_comments: Priya Nambiar: Nice work, Riley. Please add numbers for both A100 and H100 and include end-to-end latency for chat-like workloads. Also double-check thread-safety around the zero-copy KV-cache path.

Riley Chen: Added A100/H100 tables to docs/perf/quant-optimizations.md, included end-to-end chat workload numbers in the PR description, and added a mutex in kv_cache for the fallback path; the zero-copy path uses atomics and documented assumptions about layout immutability.

Ethan Park: Can you clarify how this interacts with continuous batching? If a request is forced into a large batch we may lose the low-latency benefits. Suggest scheduler favoring small batches for latency SLAs.

Riley Chen: Scheduler changes included: a low_latency_lane that pulls small batches when fusion is enabled; added config knobs and tests to ensure throughput regression is minimal. Benchmarks show <5% throughput loss for throughput-optimized workloads when lane balancing is enabled.
Lina Gomez: CI perf test flaked once, reran and passed. Approving after addressing comments and adding telemetry for fusion hit/miss metrics.
Priya Nambiar: Approved and verified perf numbers on staging cluster. Recommend gradual rollout as documented.

release_notes: Add fused dequantization + SmoothQuant kernels for INT8 and FP8 which improve throughput (up to 1.9x in microbenchmarks) and reduce p99 latency (~25%) on common chat workloads; runtime-gated behind REDWOOD_QUANT_FUSION; scheduler and KV-cache improvements to preserve latency SLOs; staged rollout recommended.
